headline: Fixes from a fourth review

headline: Fixes from an independent review

change: What matters most: a tornado of the 10-year IRR after tax, or the first year's cash flow, with each input lowered and raised by a set amount (price paid, rent, rate, growth, voids, maintenance, deposit). The bars move as you edit the deal.

headline: Current mortgage rate
change: The default mortgage rate is 5.66%, Moneyfacts' average 5-year fixed buy-to-let rate at 75% loan to value (1 August 2026), up from June 2025's 5.29%. Rates have risen since, so enter a current quote.

headline: Labels that fit on a phone
change: The 'Prices since 1995' line labels its boom, peak, low and recovery in fewer words on a narrow screen, and leaves out a label that would overlap another (its dot stays).

headline: Labels that fit on a phone

change: The ownership, scope-of-works and refurbishment lists are two columns wide, so their longer choices aren't cut off.

change: Rounded money figures put the minus sign first, as everywhere else: the projection's cash line reads −£2k, not £−2k.

headline: Tidier forms and tables
change: The best buy-to-let table's headings and names wrap, so all fifteen columns fit on a desktop screen without scrolling sideways.

headline: Tidier forms and tables
change: On a phone, a long value such as a school's name wraps, instead of squeezing its label to one word a line.

headline: Chart labels with room to breathe

headline: Chart labels with room to breathe

headline: Chart labels with room to breathe

headline: A steadier rate slider
change: Dragging the mortgage rate slider no longer shakes the page: when a new rate adds or drops a line in the cards above (the interest relief cap near the break-even rate, say), the page scrolls to match, so the slider stays under your finger.

headline: Fixes from a sixth review
change: A listing that gives the plot in acres, or with decimals (0.12 acres (485 sq m), 485.6 sq m), no longer has its plot read as the floor area; 'would make a perfect new home' no longer ticks New build.

headline: Fixes from a sixth review
change: Reopening a saved home restores which details came from its certificate and last sale, so changing the home afterwards clears them as picking an address does.

headline: Fixes from a sixth review
change: A last sale month before 1995 or after the valuation month is refused, rather than valued at today's prices or silently dropped.

headline: Fixes from a sixth review
change: A certificate's exact build year goes to the model, as in training and the command-line tool; the list still shows the nearest band.

headline: Fixes from a sixth review
change: A limited company's rental losses still carried forward in year 10 now reduce the corporation tax on the sale.

headline: Fixes from a sixth review
change: Emptying a setting to retype it no longer refills the default as you type; area totals say when the risk allowance is taken off; a paused time-lapse shows one year throughout; the same percentage rounds the same way everywhere.

headline: Fixes from a sixth review
change: The 'why this estimate' breakdown is worked out again only when the home changes, so switching tabs or theme is about four times faster.

headline: One headline accuracy figure
change: The Accuracy tab's median error and within 10% now use the strict test the README and the comparison use, where the model only sees sales at least two months old: 8.1% and 59%. With every earlier sale it is 8.0% and 60%, as the note under them says.

headline: A rent for a new tenancy
change: The rent estimate now starts where a buyer letting today would: ONS's average of rents being paid, moved to a new tenancy by the rented mix (privately rented homes are cheaper than the average of their type) and a premium from Doncaster's rent growth. It is labelled provisional until tested on local lettings; the deal, neighbourhood returns and yields use it.

headline: Comparables adjusted to this home
change: Each comparable sale is moved to this home's floor area and location with the model itself, with the reason (for example '22% larger, location 4% cheaper'), and the adjusted sales' median sits beside the estimate.

headline: Where the details come from
change: Each detail is tagged with its source (energy certificate, Land Registry, the listing, typed in, or not given), with a count of the six key details taken from official records.

headline: Who lives nearby
change: A Census 2021 card for the postcode's neighbourhood against Doncaster and England: tenure, qualifications, students, age and cars.

headline: A one-page report
change: Print a one-page report of a home (or save it as a PDF): estimate, rent, where the details come from, adjusted comparables, the area and its Census profile.

headline: One headline everywhere
change: The line under the title and the note for homes typed in by hand now quote the same 8.1% headline as the Accuracy tab and the README (they still gave 8.0%).

headline: A street map of the comparables
change: The comparables card is now a street map drawn from Ordnance Survey open data: buildings, named roads, parks, woods, water, rail and school grounds, in the dashboard's colours. Drag to move; + and − or Ctrl + scroll to zoom to house level. Each sale sits at the centre of its postcode.

headline: Rent and yield in the estimate box
change: Under the value: the rent for a new tenancy with its likely range, gross and net yield, and monthly cash flow before and after tax at today's mortgage rate, the same deal as the Investing tab.

headline: Rates after the Bank Rate rise
change: Bank Rate 4.00% (raised 5 Nov 2026), 10-year gilt 5.16%, buy-to-let mortgage rate 5.79%, property income tax 24%/44% from April 2027 (Budget, 28 Oct 2026) with mortgage interest relief at 24%, the £65 landlord register fee, and ONS rents to September 2026 (Doncaster up 5.2% in a year).

headline: Cards side by side line up
change: Cards next to each other are now the same height.

headline: A portfolio of homes like this
change: A new card on Investing buys the deal's home as many times as you set (10 to start) and lays out a year for you owning them against a limited company keeping its profit (or repaying your loan) and paying it out as dividends: costs, interest, profit, income or corporation tax worked out on the whole portfolio, tax on taking it out, cash a month, return on your cash and the lender's rent check, with notes on portfolio lending, guarantees, selling and moving homes you already own.

headline: Company settings in the deal
change: With Limited company chosen, the deal adds the company mortgage premium (0.3 points to start) and its share of the company's running costs (£3,050 a year to start), and works out corporation tax on all the company's homes together, including on a sale.

headline: Personal tax at portfolio scale
change: Your other taxable income now always shows: it sets your band on a personal portfolio (property rates from April 2027, the personal allowance taper, the Section 24 credit) and the tax on dividends (10.75%, 35.75%, 39.35% above £500).

headline: Fixed for 2 or 5 years
change: The lender's stress test follows the fix: 5 years or more is tested at its own rate, a 2-year fix at the rate + 2 points (at least 5.5%), as the PRA's rules allow.

headline: The portfolio over the holding period, then sold
change: The portfolio card adds the whole holding period (10 years to start): rent, interest, income or corporation tax each year with losses and unrelieved interest carried forward, cash to you, the sale with capital gains tax or corporation tax on the gain, and for a company two ways out: closing it (a members' voluntary liquidation, taxed as a capital gain, median fees £4,250) or dividends in one year. Total back to you and the after-tax IRR for each, plus the equity if you keep the homes instead.

headline: Interest on your loan to the company
change: Set the interest the company pays you on your loan: a cost before corporation tax, savings income for you (starting rate for savings, personal savings allowance, savings rates rising to 24%/44%/49% from April 2027). Choose whether your money goes in as a loan (paid back tax-free first) or as share capital, and whether the company pays you what it can each year or keeps its profit.

headline: The lender's view of the whole portfolio
change: Rent cover at the stress rate and borrowing against value across every home, as portfolio lenders assess it (The Mortgage Works: 125% cover for a company, 145% for a higher-rate taxpayer, at most 75% borrowing on personally owned homes), and the weakest home on its own.

headline: Your saved homes as the portfolio
change: On the private dashboard, the portfolio can be your saved homes, each at the price and rent saved with it, with this one, instead of copies of this home.

headline: Remortgaging in the portfolio
change: Each home in the portfolio is remortgaged when its 2- or 5-year fix ends, at a rate you set (left empty, the deal's mortgage rate) with a new arrangement fee, a repayment mortgage then repaying its balance over the term left, and never in the year the homes are sold. Choose to keep the same loan, borrow back up to the deposit's loan-to-value and take the cash, or borrow back and buy more homes like this one (a company keeping its profit puts that in too). Borrowing back, and borrowing for the homes it buys, is capped by the lender's rent test; interest on borrowing above what a home cost gets no tax credit when you own it yourself (HMRC PIM2105).

headline: A tidier deal form and estimate box
change: The deal analyser's boxes are even: price and mortgage, rent and costs, ownership and tax, then portfolio and company across the full width, with shorter labels that don't wrap, at every screen size. The estimate box's rent, yield and cash flow sit in one row with the mortgage terms underneath, and the property card lines up with it.
